questions.q: For the system Ax = b, when does a unique solution x exist?
options: Only when b is the zero vector
Only when A is symmetric
When A is invertible, equivalently when det(A) ≠ 0
Always, regardless of A
questions.explain: A unique solution to Ax = b exists precisely when A is invertible, which is equivalent to det(A) being nonzero.

questions.q: What does Gaussian elimination do to solve a linear system?
options: It computes the determinant and stops
It performs row operations to reduce the augmented matrix to row-echelon form, then back-substitutes
It randomly guesses values of x until one works
It only works for diagonal matrices
questions.explain: Gaussian elimination uses row swaps, scaling, and row additions to reach echelon form, then solves for the unknowns by back-substitution from the last row upward.

questions.q: In an LU decomposition A = LU, why is it useful to factor A once when solving against many different right-hand sides b?
options: Because L and U can be reused, turning each new solve into two cheap triangular solves instead of full elimination
Because LU decomposition changes the solution for each b
Because it eliminates the need for a right-hand side entirely
Because L and U are always equal to each other
questions.explain: Once A = LU is computed, solving for a new b only requires a forward solve (Ly=b) and a back solve (Ux=y), both cheap compared to redoing elimination from scratch.

questions.q: The Cholesky decomposition A = LL^T exists if and only if A is:
options: Any square matrix
Symmetric and positive definite
Diagonal
Upper triangular
questions.explain: Cholesky decomposition requires A to be symmetric and positive definite; a covariance matrix satisfies this (assuming no perfect linear dependence among assets).

questions.q: Why is the Cholesky decomposition of a covariance matrix Σ used to simulate correlated asset returns?
options: Because Σ = LL^T, so if z is a vector of independent standard normal draws, L @ z has covariance exactly Σ
Because Cholesky decomposition removes all correlation between assets
Because L is always equal to the identity matrix
Because it converts Σ into a diagonal matrix of variances only
questions.explain: Since Σ = LL^T, transforming independent standard normal draws z by L @ z produces a vector with covariance matrix L (I) L^T = LL^T = Σ, exactly the target correlation structure.
